structured_output.summary: This is a genuinely qualified 0.2.3 release candidate, not a documented intention. The recorded evidence is the complete phase-24 gate: docs/reviews/phase-24-attempt-01.checks.json contains 73 checks, all exit_code 0, each with source_unchanged true and 21 with checkpoint bindings (including both retained .crate archives); tools/review_phase.py:215 requires that command list to equal commands_for(24) exactly, and tools/check_phase.py:193-212 defines phase 24 as the phase-23 matrix rebound to phase-24 receipts plus live_evidence.py --check, red_team_management.py --require-through-phase 24 --verify-package-receipts and check-access-release.py --phase 24 --version 0.2.3. The patch-level decision is backed by real execution rather than assertion: scripts/check-management-package.py:97-155 binds a detached-worktree clean archive to the current source fingerprint (726ed2c9…, release commit 14a67541…), requires four archive-root cargo commands on a single pinned +toolchain, five uniquely indexed external consumer runs (four examples with --features red-team, the frozen 3,820-probe consumer and the positionally bound access-policy consumer), and byte equality between archive members, the working tree and the release commit; tools/management_consumers.py pins the published 0.2.2 bytes those consumers come from. Implementation matches the plan: appended union tails sit after legacy branches and before Unknown (generated.rs:172270, 172559), the client_session discriminator decodes strictly (models/red_team_management.rs:109-117), profiling_status is validated pre-dispatch and cloned onto every page (airs/red_team/targets.rs:84-91, 350-366), and tests/red_team_management_contracts.rs proves all five response declarations, four filters across four pagination surfaces, pre-auth rejection with zero token calls, projection precedence and credential-free error formatting. Release gating layers correctly and is version-specific: check-access-release requires schema-3 proofs on both compilers with commit_fingerprint == fingerprint and HEAD ancestry, verify-publication requires an accepted current-source phase-24 readiness review before and after registry access, check-prepublication reruns both and reports publicationPerformed false, and release_delivery/observe-release require an annotated remote tag plus every configured CI context (48 Rust jobs + contracts) at terminal success. Live evidence is current-source bound and candid: a schema-2 read-only receipt with a hard transport allowlist (examples/live_qualification.rs:268-283), one verified method (OAuth) and four 403s, with qualification.json reporting liveVerified 1 of 448. The remaining gap is documentation precision around that live receipt: the only probes of the new behavior used an endpoint base path that matches no declared profile, and the packaged README still describes fresh live evidence as forthcoming. No blocker or high finding; publication, remote tag and terminal CI remain pending delivery obligations.

findings.description: The only live probes of the new management behavior targeted https://api.sase.paloaltonetworks.com/ai-red-teaming/mgmt (hardcoded at crates/scm-sdk/examples/live_qualification.rs:56 and enforced by the read-only allowlist at lines 268-283). That base path matches no declared endpoint profile: the SDK default is api.apps.paloaltonetworks.com/ai-red-teaming/mgmt-plane (crates/scm-sdk/src/constants.rs:635) and the pinned 0.86.0 spec advertises api.sase.paloaltonetworks.com/ai-red-teaming/mgmt-plane (contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0/operations.json:54); grep finds /ai-red-teaming/mgmt nowhere else in declared contracts. The disclosure in LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md:22-24, CHANGELOG.md:59-62 and the receipt limitation contrast the probed URL only with the SDK default, while both documents attribute the four 403s to permissions ("HTTP 403 permission prerequisites", "remain permission-blocked"). On an undeclared route a 403 cannot be attributed to permissions alone, so the release's only live evidence for the new filter is weaker than the prose implies.
findings.required_fix: State explicitly in docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md and the CHANGELOG 0.2.3 live paragraph that the probed base path /ai-red-teaming/mgmt is not among the six declared endpoint profiles and that the 403 responses therefore do not establish permissions as the sole blocker, or add a bounded probe of a declared profile (api.apps.../mgmt-plane or api.sase.../mgmt-plane) to the read-only allowlist and record its actual outcome in the next receipt.

findings.description: The packaged README still says the archived receipt "does not qualify the current management changes; fresh live evidence belongs to release qualification" and links only contracts/historical/0.2.2-live-evidence.json (line 92). The fresh receipt now exists and is bound by contracts/live-evidence.json. README.md is the only live-evidence statement inside the published artifact: crates/scm-sdk/Cargo.toml:11 includes only src/**, examples/**, LICENSE, NOTICE and README.md, so neither CHANGELOG.md nor docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md ships with the crate. A crates.io reader of 0.2.3 is told, conservatively but incorrectly, that no current live evidence was produced.
findings.required_fix: Name docs/checks/phase-24-live-attempt-02.json (or contracts/live-evidence.json) in README.md alongside the historical receipt and state the actual current outcome (OAuth verified; four target-list filter probes returned 403 and remain unqualified), instead of describing fresh live evidence as still forthcoming.

findings.description: contractTests/contractEvidence for the Red Team target operations changed by management 0.86.0 (list, listAll, create, get, update, probe, updateProfile) reference only crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_resources_contracts.rs. Searching contracts/ shows zero occurrences of red_team_management_contracts.rs, red_team_management_fixtures.rs or red_team_management_models.rs in contracts/qualification.json or contracts/native-operations.json, so the matrix documented as the exhaustive per-method contract-verification source of truth (docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md:6-8, README.md:38) understates coverage for exactly the behavior this release adds. The evidence exists and is hash-bound in contracts/native-fixtures/red-team-management.json.
findings.required_fix: Add the three new management contract/fixture/model suites to the affected operations' tests entries in contracts/native-operations.json and regenerate contracts/qualification.json so the per-method matrix cites the suites that actually verify the 0.86.0 behavior.

findings.description: verify_offline_delivery expects `3 if version == '0.2.2' else 2` packaged `run --locked` consumers and its example list omits red_team_management. The function is unreachable for phase 24 (line 107 skips it), but the constants are now wrong for 0.2.3: check-management-package.py binds six consumer executions (four examples, the frozen probe, access policy). A later release that re-enables this branch would under-assert or fail while looking authoritative.
findings.required_fix: Derive verify_offline_delivery's expected consumer count and example list from the schema-3 receipt bindings, or scope/rename it explicitly to the historical 0.2.1/0.2.2 proofs so it cannot be mistaken for the 0.2.3 contract.

findings.description: validate_report accepts either HISTORICAL_READ_ONLY_LIMITATIONS (three items) or READ_ONLY_LIMITATIONS (four items, including the endpoint-profile disclosure added by a5e1a74). A newly executed read-only receipt that omits the endpoint disclosure would therefore still validate, so the correction is not enforced for future runs; only the Rust example's hardcoded constant (examples/live_qualification.rs:290-295) currently guarantees it, and the string is duplicated verbatim in two languages.
findings.required_fix: Require READ_ONLY_LIMITATIONS for newly executed receipts (for example accept the three-item historical list only for the retained attempt-01 receipt digest), and bind the Python and Rust copies of the limitation text through a single checked source so they cannot drift.
